claim: Package dependencies flow inward: cli → kernel → contracts, rules → vocabulary → contracts
note: ADR-001: each package owns a single bounded concern with only the dependencies it needs — ensures packages remain independently publishable and consumers only pull what they need

claim: The official file-ledger backend writes NDJSON events by appending only — never rewrites or modifies existing entries
note: ADR-003: the ledger is an append-only event log — current state is derived by replaying events, not by reading a snapshot. Third-party backends must honor the same semantics but cannot be enforced by the TypeScript interface

claim: Ledger entry IDs are ULIDs assigned by the backend at write time, not by the caller
note: ADR-004: ULIDs provide globally unique, lexicographically sortable identifiers without a central authority — the base class stamps the ID so all backends share the same generation logic

claim: Findings use observed/resolved states with a baselined flag — baseline is a flag, not a state
note: ADR-005: the finding state machine is intentionally small — baselined is a suppression flag for first-run acceptance, not a separate state

claim: Kernel and all rules are pure: same inputs always produce the same outputs, no I/O, no randomness, no LLM calls
note: ADR-006: the kernel orchestrates fact collection and rule evaluation but never writes to the ledger, makes network calls, or invokes LLMs — evaluate() is sync and Facts → Finding[]

claim: Third-party collectors must produce the same facts for the same codebase state; Rule.evaluate() and Insight.analyze() must be sync and pure with no I/O, randomness, or LLM calls
note: ADR-007: determinism is a documented contract for third-party plugins — maat cannot enforce purity at runtime in V1, so the contract is progressive: documentation now, rule-tester assertions in V1+, worker isolation in future

claim: Finding fingerprints are SHA-256 of stable-stringified ruleId plus ruleIdentifier, assigned by the kernel
note: ADR-008: fingerprints exclude volatile fields like line numbers and columns — only durable facts participate so the same finding is reproducible across runs

claim: Axioms have a three-event lifecycle (declared, superseded, revoked) and are never in the FindingStatus state machine
note: ADR-009: axioms are manual claims with no detector origin — superseded implies a replacement exists, revoked implies the claim is no longer valid

claim: RuleBuilder is a second extension point alongside defineRule for DSL-style configuration
note: ADR-010: builders prevent invalid configurations by enforcing ordering — a layer must have a role before it can be built
